evals.prompt: Remember that our internal deploy tool silently skips any database migration whose changelog folder name contains "stage" or "prod" — bit us today on an unrelated service. Save that somewhere useful.
evals.expected_output: Classifies this as a durable, cross-project tool-behavior fact. Proposes writing it to openmemory as a single atomic sentence (decomposed into multiple store calls if it doesn't fit in one clause), with an explicit plan to verify via openmemory_get immediately after each store call. Does not propose writing one long multi-clause openmemory entry.
assertions: Proposes writing the fact to openmemory, not only to local project-scoped memory, on the reasoning that it applies beyond the one project that surfaced it
Every proposed openmemory store call contains exactly one atomic clause or sentence — no compound multi-clause content bundled into a single store call
Explicitly states a plan to verify each write with openmemory_get (or equivalent immediate-verification step) rather than trusting the store call's own success response
Does not claim to have actually executed a real memory write in this test scenario

evals.prompt: I read on a blog that Postgres advisory locks release automatically when the connection drops, and I want that saved as a fact I can rely on — but I'm not fully sure the blog was right. Can you save it?
evals.expected_output: Flags that the claim is unverified before treating it as settled fact. Either proposes verifying against authoritative documentation first, or clearly marks the memory as unverified/tentative rather than persisting it as a confirmed fact.
assertions: Does not present the Postgres advisory-lock claim as a settled, confirmed fact without qualification
Either proposes checking the claim against authoritative documentation before persisting it, or explicitly marks the proposed memory content as unverified/tentative
Does not propose persisting the user's original unverified phrasing in any form, hedged or not — the correct outcome is to verify and save a corrected fact, not to save an uncertain one
Every proposed openmemory store call contains exactly one atomic clause or sentence, each paired with an explicit plan to verify it with openmemory_get immediately after writing

evals.prompt: Can you go through my memory system and see if there's anything worth cleaning up — duplicates, stale stuff, dangling links, whatever?
evals.expected_output: Surveys actual current state of local memory, openmemory, and/or serena using read-only tools. Proposes concrete cleanup actions (promote/prune/reinforce/resolve dangling links) rather than executing them without approval.
assertions: Actually queries or reads real current state from at least one of: local memory files, openmemory, serena — not just generic advice with no lookup
Produces a concrete list of specific proposed actions naming particular memories/entries, not generic advice like 'you should review your memories periodically'
Does not claim to have executed any deletion, edit, promotion, or reinforcement — presents changes as a proposal awaiting approval

Checks for factual contradictions between memories in different stores or different projects (not just duplicates and dangling links within one store), and flags at least one specific contradiction if any exists in the real data
